on_this_day.text: The last Sumatran rhinoceros in Malaysia, Imam, dies, making the species officially extinct in the country.
Founders of Italian fashion brand Dolce & Gabbana issue an apology following a series of offensive advertisements on social media promoting a fashion show in Shanghai, China, which was canceled.
Blue Origin's New Shepard space vehicle became the first rocket to successfully fly to space and then return to Earth for a controlled, vertical landing.
Arab Spring: After 11 months of protests in Yemen, Yemeni president Ali Abdullah Saleh signs a deal to transfer power to the vice president, in exchange for legal immunity.
Bombardment of Yeonpyeong: North Korean artillery attack kills two civilians and two marines on Yeonpyeong Island, South Korea.

Bane Dome structure & cross-sections
registry.desc: A doubly plunging anticline — an arch of rock layers — under Giles County. Reference: USGS Bulletin 1839.

registry.name: The +12 mGal gravity anomaly over the dome
registry.desc: Gravity over the dome reads +12 mGal high (VT survey, 1988, 395 stations) — dense rock below. Re-surveys would appear here.

registry.name: Narrows fault — trace, displacement ~4 km
registry.desc: The fault bounding the dome on the northwest; rock offset about 4 km along it.

registry.name: Saltville fault — trace, displacement ~8 km
registry.desc: The fault bounding the dome on the southeast; rock offset about 8 km. Gypsum and salt country.

registry.name: St. Clair fault system
registry.desc: The dome formed at the footwall edge of this fault system.

registry.name: Pulaski thrust sheet — 80 km displacement
registry.desc: A colossal sheet of rock shoved ~80 km northwest — the big structure southeast of the dome.

registry.name: Rome Formation décollement
registry.desc: The weak shale layer, deep down, that the whole stack of rock slides on.

registry.name: Strader #1 well
registry.desc: The crest well on the dome; its conodont fossils rewrote the dome’s story in 1979 (Perry et al., AAPG).

registry.name: Knox Group beneath the dome — windows (fensters)
registry.desc: At Price Mountain the cover is eroded through, opening windows into the Knox limestone beneath.

registry.name: Pulaski sheet "horses"
registry.desc: Rootless slices of the Pulaski sheet stranded inside the fensters.

registry.name: Devonian black shale — gas-prospective
registry.desc: Organic black shale under the dome; its fractures can trap gas.

registry.name: Rome trough
registry.desc: An ancient rift basin buried underneath everything — the oldest chapter of the stack.

registry.name: Conodont color alteration
registry.desc: Fossil teeth changed color with heat — proof these rocks were cooked into the gas window.

registry.name: Giles County seismic zone — Virginia’s most active
registry.desc: The ground here moves more than anywhere else in Virginia. Live via the USGS local feed.

registry.name: The 1897 Giles County earthquake (~M5.8)
registry.desc: May 31, 1897 — the largest earthquake in Virginia’s recorded history, right here in Giles County.

registry.name: Micro-quakes within 100 km of Pembroke
registry.desc: The small end of the same restlessness — live subset of the USGS local watch.

registry.name: Central VA seismic zone — 2011 Mineral M5.8 context
registry.desc: The 2011 Mineral quake’s zone, east of here — the regional comparison.

registry.name: Swarm watch on Narrows / Saltville traces
registry.desc: Clustering in the local feed, computed daily — the traces to watch are the dome’s own faults.

registry.name: Quarry blast vs quake discrimination
registry.desc: Many small local "quakes" in catalogs are quarry blasts — shallow, weekday, daytime. Read local events with that in mind.

registry.name: Radon — fault-fractured rock pathways
registry.desc: Fractured rock along the faults gives radon gas a path up. EPA zone data is the wire source.

registry.name: Telluric / earth-current research along the faults
registry.desc: Natural earth currents along fault lines — a research thread, no live feed yet.

registry.name: Mountain Lake — the vanishing lake
registry.desc: One of two natural lakes in Virginia; it drained away in 2008 and refilled around 2020. Level record via USGS reporting.

registry.name: Rock City boulder field, Mountain Lake
registry.desc: A field of house-sized sandstone boulders near the lake — the mountain slowly coming apart.

registry.name: Karst sinkholes — Giles / Bland reports
registry.desc: Limestone country dissolves from below; new sinkhole reports are the wire signal.

registry.name: Cave systems — New River Cave, Tawney’s Cave
registry.desc: Known cave systems in the limestone around the dome.

registry.name: Limestone springs & spring flow on the dome flanks
registry.desc: Springs line the dome’s flanks where limestone meets shale; flow gauging is not yet wired.

registry.name: Saltville salt — brine at the fault system’s edge
registry.desc: Salt and brine at Saltville, on the same fault system — worked since the Civil War era and long before.

registry.name: Fault-line springs — Hot Springs & Warm Springs VA
registry.desc: Warm water rises along deep faults east of here — the same plumbing, showing at the surface.

registry.name: The New River — ancient, north-flowing, cuts the dome country
registry.desc: One of the oldest rivers on Earth, flowing north through the dome country. Live gauges on the Earth card.

registry.name: Dismal Creek & its falls
registry.desc: A cold mountain creek and falls in the county’s east.

registry.name: Acid mine drainage & coal seeps, regional
registry.desc: Old coal country drainage — a water-quality wire item for the region.

registry.name: Methane seeps — gas country above the shale
registry.desc: Gas country: seeps above the Devonian shale are reported, not instrumented.

registry.name: UAP reports over the New River Valley (NUFORC)
registry.desc: Public report counts for the valley — reports are data about reports, labeled as such.

registry.name: Fireballs over the valley (AMS)
registry.desc: Bright meteors over the valley — the global fireball feed is live; valley reports ride the wire.

registry.name: Brown Mountain Lights — NC
registry.desc: The regional light anomaly across the line in North Carolina — reports layer.

registry.name: Bigfoot reports — Giles / Appalachian VA (BFRO)
registry.desc: Public report database entries for the county and region — reports, labeled as reports.

registry.name: Mothman corridor — Point Pleasant WV
registry.desc: Upriver on the same river system — the 1966–67 Point Pleasant reports are the regional reference case.

registry.name: Mystery booms & hums reported in VA
registry.desc: Unexplained boom/hum reports statewide — wire item, checked against quarry and quake records first.

registry.name: Aeromagnetic anomaly maps, Giles County (USGS)
registry.desc: Flown magnetic surveys map the buried structure — the dome shows in magnetics as well as gravity.

registry.name: The 1988 gravity baseline — 395 stations
registry.desc: Moses 1988 (VT thesis): the gravity baseline every later survey compares against.

registry.name: Celanese, Narrows — industry in the fault valley
registry.desc: The plant sits in the river gap the geology cut — industry follows the corridor.

registry.name: Gypsum — US Gypsum / Plasterco on the Saltville fault
registry.desc: Gypsum mining rides the Saltville fault’s evaporite beds.

registry.name: Gas wells & permits over the dome (VA DMME records)
registry.desc: State records of wells and permits over the structure.

registry.name: Mountain Valley Pipeline corridor
registry.desc: The pipeline crosses this county — its corridor crosses the dome country too.

registry.name: Norfolk Southern through the Narrows
registry.desc: Rail through the river gap — the corridor again.

registry.name: The Narrows gap itself
registry.desc: The river cut through the ridge; town, rail, road, and plant all thread the gap geology made.

registry.name: Saltville ice-age fossils — mastodon & mammoth
registry.desc: Ice-age giants preserved in the Saltville salt marshes — an active paleontology site.

registry.name: Devonian shale fossils
registry.desc: The black shale carries its own fossil record.

registry.name: Cambrian Rome Formation outcrops
registry.desc: The oldest rock in the stack, exposed where the rivers cut deep enough.

registry.name: Knox limestone fossil sites — trilobites, brachiopods
registry.desc: Sea-floor fossils in the Knox limestone — this was an ocean once.
